title: CLICK TO CALL CONGRESS: Stop the Cuts. Protect Black Futures

sponsor.name: State of the People. Los Angeles Action Hub.

description:
# CALL CONGRESS: Stop the Cuts. Protect Black Futures

## This is a national call to action.

Congress is advancing budget rollbacks that will directly harm Black communities — cutting healthcare, housing, food access, education equity, maternal health, and youth job training.

These are not policy tweaks. These are direct attacks on our futures.

**Sign up to take action. Then click to call. You'll get everything you need — including who to contact and what to say.**

---

## What Happens After You Sign Up

1. You’ll be directed to **call the U.S. Capitol Switchboard**  
   - **Phone Number:** (202) 224-3121  
   - Ask to speak to your **U.S. Representative** or **Senators** by name or ZIP code

2. You’ll get a **sample call script** (below)  
3. You’ll help stop harmful cuts — and demand what we’re owed

---

## Programs at Risk

- **Job Corps** – job access for Black youth  
- **Section 8 Housing Vouchers** – keeping families housed  
- **WIC & SNAP** – food access for mothers and children  
- **Medicaid** – healthcare for our elders, kids, and disabled neighbors  
- **Black Maternal Health Programs** – doulas, midwives, and prevention  
- **Community Violence Intervention (CVI)** – proven harm reduction strategies  
- **Public Schools (Title I)** – schools serving Black and low-income youth  
- **Pell Grants & Loan Forgiveness** – education access and debt justice  
- **Environmental Justice** – clean air, clean water, healthy communities

---

## Need to Look Up Your Rep?

- [Find your Representative – House.gov](https://www.house.gov/representatives/find-your-representative)  
- [Find your Senators – Senate.gov](https://www.senate.gov/senators/senators-contact.htm)

---

## Call Script

Hi, my name is [Your Name], and I live in [City], [ZIP].

I’m calling to demand that you vote NO on any federal budget that cuts funding for programs our communities depend on — including Job Corps, Medicaid, Section 8, SNAP, maternal health care, and community violence intervention.

These are essential services. Cutting them would cause real harm.

We demand equity, repair, and investment — not more harm.

Vote no on these cuts. Protect Black futures.


---

## Why It Matters

These budget proposals are part of a larger campaign to strip resources from our people, dismantle our safety nets, and erase our right to thrive.

But we are not silent. We organize.  
**Click to call. Speak your truth. Hold the line.**

title: Sign the Letter: Tell Congress to Stop the Cuts. Protect Black Futures

sponsor.name: State of the People. Los Angeles Action Hub.

description:
# Sign the Letter: Tell Congress to Stop the Cuts. Protect Black Futures

**Add your name now. Demand Congress vote NO on budget cuts that harm Black communities.**

Congress is moving to slash funding for the programs Black communities rely on — including housing, health care, food access, education, maternal health, and youth opportunity.

This is not abstract. This is direct harm.

We deserve investment, not erasure.  
We deserve equity, not excuses.  
We deserve repair, not rollback.

**Sign the letter and tell Congress: Protect what we’ve built. Fund what we need. Stop the cuts now.**

---

## What’s At Risk

- **Job Corps** – youth job training and employment  
- **Medicaid** – health care for low-income families and elders  
- **Section 8 Housing Vouchers** – rental and housing support  
- **WIC & SNAP** – food assistance for pregnant people and children  
- **Black Maternal Health Programs** – doulas, midwives, prenatal care  
- **Community Violence Intervention (CVI)** – grassroots safety and healing  
- **Public Education (Title I)** – schools serving Black youth  
- **Pell Grants & Loan Relief** – access to higher education  
- **Environmental Justice Programs** – clean air and water in Black communities

title: Sign Now: Advance Reparations for a Just and Healed California

sponsor.name: State of the People. Los Angeles Action Hub.

description:
#Sign the Form: Advance Reparations for a Just and Healed California

**Add your name. Call on California lawmakers to deliver floor votes on key reparations bills — for repair, redress, and a future rooted in justice.**

---

California has the opportunity to lead — not just in words, but through policy rooted in truth, equity, and repair.

Right now, three key bills inspired by the state’s Reparations Task Force are moving through the legislature. We’re calling for immediate floor votes to move these bills forward.

**This is a demand for action. For repair. For redress. For a just and healed California.**

Sign the form today and tell California legislators: **deliver floor votes for repair, redress, and Black futures.**

---

## What’s at Stake

- **SB 518** – *Establishes the California Reparations Bureau*  
  Creates a permanent state agency to coordinate and implement reparations-related programs for descendants of enslaved Black Americans.  
  [Read the bill →](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billNavClient.xhtml?bill_id=202520260SB518)

- **SB 437** – *Creates Genealogical Standards for Eligibility*  
  Directs the California State University system to develop lineage-based standards to determine fair eligibility for reparations.  
  [Read the bill →](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billNavClient.xhtml?bill_id=202520260SB437)

- **AB 57** – *Provides Homebuyer Assistance for Descendants*  
  Offers targeted homeownership support for descendants of enslaved Black Americans — a step toward housing justice and wealth repair.  
  [Read the bill →](https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/billNavClient.xhtml?bill_id=202520260AB57)

---

## Why It Matters

California can set the national standard — but only if it chooses to act.

These bills aren’t about the past. They are about **repairing systemic harm**, restoring opportunity, and **building a future where Black communities are valued, resourced, and free.**

No more delay. No more symbolic gestures.  
**We need floor votes. We need action. We need repair.**

title: Disappeared in America Visual Action
description:
**In America, the government doesn’t get to grab people off the streets, skip the courtroom, and send them straight to a foreign prison.** Disappeared in America is a national day of action to stand up for the rule of law and confront the Trump administration’s illegal abductions, detentions, and deportations of people like Kilmar Abrego Garcia, Rui Marras, and Juan Maldonado Zuniga. 

🚨**On Thursday, June 26th, we’re showing up at courthouses and town squares across the country to say: in America, we don’t let the government disappear people. That’s not who we are.**🚨

Americans believe in rule of law —and the courts are saying that due process is required. If a president can ignore the courts and disappear lawful residents, there is no limit to what can come next. President Trump has said he wants to abduct and deport U.S. citizens. If this isn’t stopped now, no one is safe.

**On June 26th we are launching a national photo petition day where people will take photos with posters of those who have been disappeared and flood social media with the truth.** 

A key focal point of this campaign will be to call on local sheriffs to refuse to cooperate with directives from ICE to engage in federal immigration enforcement, such as renting jail beds to ICE, participating in immigration raids, and transferring people to ICE detentions.  Sheriffs have wide discretion in how much they cooperate with ICE. Participation in federal immigration activities places additional burden on sheriffs’ offices and can erode local community trust in local law enforcement.

_A core principle behind all Disappeared in America events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values._

The Big Ugly Bill has passed the house and now is the time to make your voice heard. The bill calls for devastating cuts to Medicaid, SNAP, and the safety net, all to pay for tax breaks for the ultra-wealthy. Pennsylvania voters, like voters in other states, strongly support these programs, and with good reason. Medicaid provides critical support for millions of Pennsylvanians.

The reconciliation bill will terminate healthcare coverage for around 13 million Americans and kick approximately 3 million Americans off of SNAP. While new requirements for the state to help pay for the SNAP program would result in new expenditures for the state of $226 million to over a billion. The bill does all this harm while adding $2.4 trillion to the federal deficit.

This event is open to everyone. Join Pennsylvanians Together and the Pennsylvania Policy Center, for a real conversation about proposals that could harm Pennsylvanians, and what we can do about them. We will have experts to discuss what these cuts mean for us and our communities as well as explain what you can do to fight the cuts.

title: Grassroots Leadership Training: Launch an Action Team to Build Electoral Power in Racine County
description:
How can you fight back against the extreme Republican agenda and create a better future where everyone in Wisconsin can thrive? Become a leader of a neighborhood action team! 

Since 2017, neighborhood action teams have been monumental in electing Democrats in close races in Wisconsin. That’s why we’re launching teams in Racine County to take our organizing to the next level! By building community and having powerful conversations with our neighbors this summer, we’ll be prepared to take on Republicans and win elections up and down the ballot in 2026. 

Through this training, you will learn the skills and strategy to effectively launch and lead your neighborhood action team. Plus, you’ll be matched with other motivated co-leaders in your area to work together and receive ongoing support from the Democratic Party of Wisconsin.

Note: This training is designed for volunteers who can commit to being a co-leader of a neighborhood action team in Caledonia, Mt. Pleasant, or the city of Racine. If you would like to take action as a member instead or are located in a different county, check out our [other events](https://www.mobilize.us/wisdems/). Questions? title: Speak Out! Support Affordable Housing! Attend County Commission Hearing
description:

**In America, we don’t put up with would-be kings.**
NO KINGS is a national day of action and mass mobilization in response to increasing authoritarian excesses and corruption from President Trump and his allies. We’ve watched as they’ve cracked down on free speech, detained people for their political views, threatened to deport American citizens, and defied the courts. They’ve done this all while continuing to serve and enrich their billionaire allies.


🚨**On Saturday, June 14, we’re taking to the streets nationwide. We’re not gathering to feed his ego. We’re building a movement that leaves him behind.**🚨


The flag doesn’t belong to the Trump administration. It belongs to us. We’re not watching history happen. We’re making it.


**On June 14th, we’re showing up everywhere he isn’t—to say no thrones, no crowns, no kings.**
Check out nokings.org for more information.

*A core principle behind all No Kings events is a commitment to nonviolent action. We expect all participants to seek to de-escalate any potential confrontation with those who disagree with our values.*

title: Sorting Soup: Turning Ideas Into Action - Join Weekly - every Tuesday & Thursday,  Zoom @4PM central
description:
#### Sorting Soup: Turning Ideas Into Action - Join Weekly - every Tuesday & Thursday,  Zoom @4PM central

_Feeling overwhelmed by the constant stream of ideas, strategies, and information in the pro-democracy movement? You’re not alone._

That’s why we created Sorting Soup—a twice-weekly space to process, connect, and turn information into real-world impact. Inspired by the dynamic NWSOFA 9am Coffee & Conversation network, Sorting Soup is your opportunity to ground yourself, build community, and decide what’s truly worth your time and energy.

#### Let us know you will be attending … RSVP here-> https://mobilize.us/s/1162kb

Join us every Tuesday and Thursday at 4 PM (CST), starting June 10th. Each session begins with a Decompression Hour, where we check in, share what’s on our minds, and spot the patterns emerging across our work. Then, we dive deep into a timely topic—something urgent, overlooked, or full of potential. Whether you’re ready to research, present, or just ask great questions, your voice is welcome.

We wrap up with a Deep Dive Debrief, assigning research tasks, brainstorming future speakers, and mapping out next steps. Our goal? Not just understanding, but activation. Sorting Soup is about thinking together—and then bringing those insights back to our communities to inspire real change.

### Ready to stir the soup with us? Click here for the Sorting Soup Mobilize link!

_Bring your curiosity, your questions, and your passion for democracy. Let’s turn information overload into collective action—one session at a time._

title: Union the Film Viewing Fundraiser
description:
Union the Film
Join us for a special screening of the award-winning documentary UNION!

**Tickets for this event are available through Betterworld:  https://strike-our-rights.betterworld.org/events/union-viewing-portland-june**

UNION chronicles the extraordinary efforts of an unlikely group of warehouse workers, including Chris Smalls, as they launch a grassroots union campaign at an Amazon fulfillment center in Staten Island, New York.

Proceeds from this viewing go directly to Strike For Our Rights' strike fund, supporting striking workers fighting for living wages and equity, like those in this film.

Here's what some striking workers have said about our work:

"The strike assistance impacted my life in a huge way. It gave me some relief and hope that I could make it. I don’t have family so I have no one to ask for support and having this as a resource is beyond amazing. Words can’t really describe how it affected me, but it truly was life saving." - Kristin F. (IATSE)

"Because of your support I was able to stay current on my rent that month." - Jess (IAW)

"Please if you can spare anything to help assist with the strike fund it would be greatly appreciated. Being on strike is such a scary time in life. I’m currently on strike and my stress level is sky high. I’m a single parent with no other income." - L.S. (CWA)

"Unless you've been through a strike, you don't know what it's like. It's mentally and physically challenging, every bit of support helps." - Mr. Jones (Local 36g)

Strike For Our Rights is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit whose mission is to support, organize, and promoting striking as a means of advocating for justice, equity, and systemic change. Learn more at www.strikeforourrights.org
